issues.area: correctness / concurrency: L5K-R18 is not fully met. A job promoted during the funnel's RE-S40 re-read answers its user-initiated asker before the readers' snapshot holds the asset (R-STO-13, ARCHITECTURE §5)

The REENTRANCY comments at :262-265 and :190 do not name the lane. Docs that claim the opposite: EnginePresence.swift:226-229, docs/MIGRATION.md:197 ("that of a job a user-initiated request joined, is installed before the call returns"), docs/adr-drafts/k.md L5K-R18.
issues.problem:
In `storedLocation`, the lane re-read (L5K-R18) runs before the re-arm (L5K-R16). When that re-arm actually reads the store, which it does unless the alarm already wakes within 2 × interval, an `ensureAvailable` can join the job during the await. Its answer then comes from the store with no install.

Timeline:
1. During migration, a prefetch job's pre-transfer read adopts asset A at `.bulk`. The publication is coalesced, so an install is due.
2. The job's lane is re-read and is still `.prefetch`, so there is no second ask.
3. `refreshStoreDeadlineAfterPublish()` awaits `store.nextDeadline()`.
4. Meanwhile an `ensureAvailable([A])` that read its planning view before the bind (A absent) finishes its off-actor plan. It registers its `.ensure` group, and `pump` joins the job, which is promoted to `.userInitiated`.
5. The re-read resumes and returns A's location. `answeredFromStore` answers the ensure group from the store.
6. `ensureAvailable` returns `present == 1`, while `lookup`, `existingLocalURL` and `hasAsset` miss A until the trailing install.

Probe PE5 makes this deterministic. A gated `SyncPlanning` (`EngineHarness.make(planner:)`) holds ensureAvailable's plan, and the existing seam `holdNextStoreDeadlineRead()` holds the re-read after the store answered. Result on HEAD: `heldRead=true laneAtHold=prefetch viewSawAbsent=true promotedDuringHold=true present=1 unseenAtReturn=1`. It failed 9 of 9 runs (2 of them under TSan) and passes 5 of 5 with the re-arm moved before the re-read.

The window is narrow, and the miss lasts at most about one or two install intervals (0.1 to 0.2 s), but it breaks the invariant L5K-R18 states ("a user-initiated asker never returns before the readers' snapshot holds the asset"). Probe source: .build-verify-k-c3-correct/pkg/Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/VerifierKC3EngineProbe.swift (`pe5PromotionDuringTheReRead`, `VKC3GatedPlanner`). Copy it before the orchestrator clears .build-verify-*.

Already tried in a scratch copy: PE5 passes 5 of 5, and EngineLegacyMigrationTransferTests (18) pass.
- Complete fix: in `answeredFromStore`, after the loop, when any id was adopted at bulk urgency and `self.state.jobs[transfer]?.lane == .userInitiated`, make one `adoptLegacyNow(lastAdoptedID, urgency: .userInitiated)` before `answerPresentMembers`. issues.area: requirements / L5K-R16 class broken by the L5K-R17 fix (R-STO-13, ARCHITECTURE §5 trailing install, MIGRATION.md §4)
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetStorage/Migration/LegacyPhases.swift:395 (the batch publishes at .bulk), :402-412 (the L5K-R17 wait, inside the same call), :415 (phases 3-4 follow in the same call); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineRuns.swift:1080/1094 (the RE-S40 re-arm runs only after migrateLegacy returns); docs/MIGRATION.md:193-198; docs/adr-drafts/k.md:889-891 (invariant), :914 (migrateLoop row), :29 (k-7 row)
issues.problem:
performMigrateLegacy publishes the batch's adoptions at .bulk. Inside the install window that only marks the trailing install due. Since L5K-R17 the same call then waits for an adopt-on-demand of the last claimed file, and the engine's re-arm runs only after the call returns. So while the batch waits, nothing puts the store's deadline on the heap, and the batch's adopted files stay out of the readers' snapshot (lookup, existingLocalURL, hasAsset) until that on-demand adoption ends. That is one hash on a device, and unbounded while a unit is held in tests.

Probe KC3-WAITWINDOW, 3 of 3 runs at HEAD (installInterval 0.1, a prefetch job holding the last file, the batch waiting): storedByBatch=3 unseenAtWait=3 storeNextAtWait=1.0s heapAtWait=nil. After time.advance(by: 1) and runStoreWork, now=2.0s, unseenAfterWindow=3, heapAfter=nil, storeNext still 1.0s, so the install is 1 s overdue with no alarm armed.

This breaks the ruled invariant: the heap holds a deadline no later than nextDeadline(), and nothing stays out of the snapshot longer than one interval. MIGRATION.md §4 promises within snapshotInstallInterval. The tripwire cannot see it, because the migration loop is running, and no test covers it. The same mechanism applies after the last batch's publication during phases 3-4 of that call. That part is by code reading only and was not probed.
issues.fix:
Tests first: an engine test in KC3-WAITWINDOW's shape (rateLimitedLaunch, the job's hash held, the store's line 'a migration batch waits for an adopt-on-demand' reached, the clock past the window, every batch-adopted id in harness.sink.installed). The probe is at .build-verify-k-c3-reqs/pkg/Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/VerifierKC3WaitWindowProbe.swift.

Then one of two fixes:
(a) Within LegacyPhases.swift, already authorised (L5K-R13/R17): a call that published (adoptedAny) installs its own adoptions at once, with publishSnapshot(urgency: .userInitiated), before its first awaitLegacyFlight and before finishLegacyMigration, since no engine re-arm can follow until it returns. That costs one extra install per such batch. My prototype FIXW (the wait half only) passes the probe and the engine L5K-R1 file (18), the store race file (10) and MigrationLaunchShimTests (4).
(b) An L5K-R17 amendment: return right after a publication, so the engine re-arms, and let the next call wait or finish. That is at most one extra call.

Add the case to the L5K-R16 enumeration's migrateLegacy row and correct MIGRATION.md §4 and k.md.

The test assumes the held batch is at legacy0's hash, so the job takes legacy1 from the queue. When startHoldingMigration's last release meets legacy0's unit, a case heldJoinLaunch's comment documents, the batch holds legacy1 itself. issues.problem:
The test assumes the held batch is on legacy0, so the job's adoption takes legacy1 from the queue. `startHoldingMigration`'s own doc allows the migration to be held at a later file instead.

Probe DIAG-R17 ran the test's exact shape in 40 launches. In 4 of them, `pendingAfterStart=1`: the batch held legacy1, the job joined the batch's file, and the batch finished alone. That gives 0 calls whatever L5K-R17 does, so the test passes without testing anything.

Its 64 round trips also detect a missing store wait only by chance. Under a mutant without the wait, the window saw at most 1 call in all 16 launches where the premise held, and only `calls <= 2` failed (10 of 20). A long release loop sees 35 to 46 calls with the wait removed and 0 on HEAD (probes DIAG2-R17 and PSPIN-c3). Caveat: the mutant's environment lookup slows each call, so the real pre-fix code is likely caught more often; the fixer recorded 10 calls on 390523a. The store test, which asserts its premise, remains the deterministic pin.
issues.fix: After the start, add `try #require(EngineLegacyMigrationTransferTests.pending(harness, catalog).count == catalog.count)`, or use 3 files and give the job the last pending one. issues.area: docs accuracy: the 'within one install interval' bound ignores RE-S40's O(1) shortcut
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EnginePresence.swift:226; docs/MIGRATION.md:194-197; docs/adr-drafts/k.md L5K-R16 invariant paragraph; shortcut in Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineTimers.swift `refreshStoreDeadlineAfterPublish`
issues.problem:
`refreshStoreDeadlineAfterPublish` skips the read while the heap's store deadline is within 2 × max(0.05, interval).

Timeline: a commit deadline is already armed at now + 0.19 s. An install at now opens the window. A bulk adoption at now + ε marks the trailing install due at now + 0.1. The shortcut skips the read, and the alarm installs at now + 0.19.

So coalesced adoptions reach the lookups within about two install intervals (0.2 s by default), not one. In that time the heap's store deadline can be later than `nextDeadline()`. L5K-R16 deliberately kept the shortcut (F-12), so this is wording only.
issues.fix: Say "within about two install intervals (0.2 s by default)" in all three places, or describe the shortcut's bound where the L5K-R16 invariant is stated.

issues.problem: The table of every engine store call leaves out `availability(of:)`. It is a synchronous read that cannot publish, so no re-arm is needed. Only the enumeration's completeness is affected.

**Gates and runs: every command in the task passes.**
- `--quick`: `VERIFY: PASS`.
- The release build, the unsafe and docs gates, and the generic iOS build pass.
- The compatibility target passed 3 times and once under TSan, with no ThreadSanitizer report.

**The earlier blockers are fixed.** I reproduced each with probes of my own, under my scratch path. Each passes on HEAD, and fails under a mutant that removes the fix (a switch set from the environment, in a scratch copy only).
- L5K-C2-00 and C2-02. Probe PE1: a bulk sync adopts 150 files during migration. On HEAD every file is seen once the install window has passed. With only the funnel's re-arm removed, the readers see none of 149 and the engine's heap has no store entry, while the store reports 1.1 s.
- L5K-C2-03. Probe PE2b runs the sync's own trailing install first, then lets migration adopt 30 pages. On HEAD all 30 are seen and the tripwire is clean. With the loop's re-arm removed, none of the 30 is ever seen and the tripwire fires.
- L5K-C2-01, store level. Probes PS3-c3a (two adoptions on demand hold the last two files), PS3-c3b (one is deferred back to the queue) and PS3-c3d (close() during the wait) all hold on HEAD. With the wait loop removed, all three return early.
- L5K-C2-01, engine level. Probe PSPIN-c3 (two jobs hold the last two files) sees 0 `migrateLegacy` calls on HEAD and 20/44/46 with the wait removed.

**Concurrency review.**
- The crossed-answer logic (`applyStoreDeadline`, keeping the earlier deadline) cannot lose a deadline. At worst it causes one early alarm per crossing.
- Every await the close-out added has a REENTRANCY comment (script over the diff: 0 missing).
- PE3 runs a prefetch beside a migration that runs at its own pace, over 12 launches. Every file was seen, nothing was downloaded, and the tripwire was checked and clean in all 12.
- The new tests and my probes ran twice under TSan with no report.

**The blocking issue.** L5K-R18's invariant still has a window, proven by probe PE5: it fails 9 of 9 runs on HEAD, 2 of them under TSan. The engine re-reads a job's lane before its last await, the re-arm L5K-R16 added. An `ensureAvailable` that joins the job during that await is answered while the readers' snapshot does not yet hold the asset. Moving the re-arm before the lane re-read (tried in a scratch copy) passes PE5 5 of 5 and the 18 tests of the L5K-R1 file.
